title: Track job applications in one clear pipeline | SearchBreaker
description: See every application and next step in one organized job-search pipeline. Learn the workflow, its controls and what you can review before applying.

blocks.headline: Track job applications in one clear pipeline
blocks.lead: Know which resume you sent, where each application stands and what to do next. SearchBreaker keeps the job, the dates, the resume version and the follow-ups in one place.

media.label: Application pipeline
media.alt: Concept of the application pipeline with the resume version and next action on each card
media.caption: Each card shows the resume version and the next action.

blocks.reassurance: Your applications stay yours to edit and export.

blocks.heading: See the whole application pipeline
blocks.lead: Switch between a board by stage and a table you can scan. Both show the same applications.

blocks.heading: Keep every application’s details together
blocks.lead: Everything you need for a follow-up or an interview lives on the application, not in a spreadsheet.

items.title: Job and description
items.text: The posting and its description saved with the application, even if the listing disappears.

items.title: Date and resume version
items.text: When you applied and exactly which resume version you sent.

items.title: Contacts and notes
items.text: Recruiters, hiring managers and the notes from every conversation.

blocks.heading: Know your next action
blocks.lead: Every application carries one next step, so nothing waits on your memory.

points.title: Set follow-up dates
points.text: Choose when to follow up and see what is due, in order of date.

points.title: Update the stage yourself
points.text: Move an application forward as things change. You always control the status.

points.title: See what is stalled
points.text: Spot applications with no activity so you can follow up or move on.

blocks.heading: Start with the tracker
blocks.lead: You can begin with one application. What is available today is labeled.

items.title: Add an application by hand
items.text: Enter a job, date and resume version directly into the tracker.

items.title: Import earlier applications
items.text: Bring in applications you tracked elsewhere. Supported formats will be listed when import is verified.

faqs.a: You can start with a single application and add detail as you go. The tracker is meant to save time, not to become another spreadsheet to maintain.
Import is planned. Supported formats will be published when it is verified. Until then, none are promised.
Each application records the exact resume version and the date, so you can answer that question in seconds.

faqs.q: How is this different from a spreadsheet template?
faqs.a: A template is a file you maintain yourself. The tracker keeps the resume version, dates and follow-ups connected to the rest of your search.

faqs.q: What do the status names mean?
faqs.a: Each stage describes where the application stands, and you can rename or reorder stages to match your own process.
It is at concept stage. Join the waitlist to hear when it is ready to test.
